blocks.text: The Questions We Get Asked Most

items.a: There are three work visas. Engineer/Humanities — Graduate/Undergraduate degree, 1 year of experience and N5, age 22–40. SSW — N4 and a skill test, minimum SSC, age 18–35. TITP — N5, ongoing language study, minimum SSC, age 18–35. There's a separate student visa for studying.
items.q: Which visa is right for me to go to Japan?

items.a: Yes. You can work 28 hours a week part-time alongside your studies — about 120 hours a month. Hourly pay in Japan is typically ¥1000–1200.
items.q: Can I work on a student visa in Japan?

items.a: There are three sessions a year — April, July, and October. It's best to start a few months ahead for paperwork and language prep.
items.q: When are the admission sessions in Japan?

items.a: No, every visa requires a minimum language level — N5 for TITP and Engineer visas, N4 for SSW. We provide structured training targeting JLPT/JFT/NAT.
items.q: Can I go without knowing Japanese?

items.a: On an Engineer/Humanities visa, you can bring your spouse after 3 months. SSW-2 also allows bringing family. This isn't available on a TITP visa.
On an Engineer/Humanities visa, you can apply for citizenship after 5 years. On an SSW visa, that opportunity comes after 10 years of work.
items.q: Can I live in Japan permanently?
